name: GVA-63+
title: High gain, high IP3 monolithic amplifier, 50 Ω, 0.01 to 6 GHz
summary: GVA-63+ is a 50 Ω broadband gain block built on an InGaP HBT process, working from 10 MHz to 6 GHz in a SOT-89 (DF782) package. It gives about 21 dB of gain and +35 dBm output IP3 at 0.8 GHz, and its input and output are matched to 50 Ω on the die, so the parts around it are DC-blocking capacitors, an RF choke for bias and a supply bypass capacitor. It runs from a 5 V device voltage at a typical 69 mA, fed through the RF output pin.
key_figures: 21.1 dB typ, 19.0 dB min at 0.8 GHz; 15.9 dB typ at 6 GHz

rows: DF782 (SOT-89), plastic, exposed paddle, matte-tin lead finish
tape and reel F55; 7" reels of 20, 50, 100, 200, 500 or 1K devices

pins.name: RF-IN
pins.function: Amplifier input. Needs a series DC-blocking capacitor sized for the operating band.

pins.function: Ground. Place vias to the ground plane at this pin to keep ground inductance low.

pins.name: RF-OUT and DC-IN
pins.function: Amplifier output, which also takes the DC supply. It sits at the device voltage, so the load connects through a DC-blocking capacitor and the supply arrives through an RF choke.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Ground; the package tab. Place vias to the ground plane under it to keep ground inductance low.

circuits.title: Characterization test circuit
circuits.description: The bench set-up behind the electrical table. The amplifier sits on the TB-313 board; a BLK-18+ DC block feeds its input, and a ZX85-12G-S+ bias tee on pin 3 brings in the +5 V supply and passes the RF on to the output connector.
notes: Gain, return loss, P1dB, OIP3 and noise figure are measured with an Agilent N5242A PNA-X network analyzer.
Gain and return loss: input power −25 dBm.
OIP3: two tones 1 MHz apart, each at 0 dBm at the output.

circuits.title: Recommended application circuit
circuits.description: The amplifier needs no matching parts. A series capacitor blocks DC at the input and another at the output; the supply reaches pin 3 through an RF choke, and a bypass capacitor holds the supply end of the choke at RF ground.
notes: Ibias flows from Vcc through the RFC into pin 3; the voltage at pin 3 is Vd.

operation.text: An InGaP HBT die in the SOT-89 plastic package (case style DF782), which gives very good thermal performance. RoHS compliant; the + suffix marks RoHS compliance.
Both ports are matched internally to 50 Ω. Input and output return loss stays between 12 and 25 dB up to 6 GHz with no external matching parts.

There is no separate supply pin: DC enters at pin 3 together with the RF output, through an RF choke from Vcc. Pin 3 is limited to +5.7 V absolute; for continuous use keep the device voltage at 5.2 V or less. Typical bias is 69 mA at 5.0 V, and the current moves 0.040 mA per mV of device voltage.
The 10 MHz lower edge depends on the external parts: the coupling capacitors and the bias choke set the low-frequency cut-off.
Output IP3 sits about 16 dB above output P1dB up to 0.8 GHz.
Thermal resistance from junction to the ground lead is 91 °C/W. The operating temperature range, −40 °C to +85 °C, is referred to the ground lead.
Ground pins 2 and 4 return through vias to the ground plane to keep ground inductance low; the recommended land pattern is PL-255.
Evaluation board: TB-410-63+. Environmental ratings: ENV08T1. S-parameter data (S2P) and X-parameter models are offered for the part.

Uses listed for the part: base station infrastructure, portable wireless, CATV and DBS, MMDS and wireless LAN, LTE; also driver stages in up-converter chains for complex waveforms and in linearized transmitters. Offered as a replacement for the RFMD SBB5089Z, with suitability in a given system left to the user.
